title: Anchor of the Soul
subtitle: Hebrews in Poems & Pictures
author: Timothy Holt
beforeYouBegin:
The letter to the Hebrews was written to people who were tired and tempted to drift. It answers them with pictures: the radiance of the sun at morning, a boat slipping its mooring, a word as sharp as light along a blade, an anchor holding below the waves, a curtain torn open. Then it opens a long roll of the faithful—Abel, Enoch, Noah building in a dry field, Abraham walking out not knowing where, Sarah, Moses, Rahab and her scarlet cord—and sets them in the stands around a runner on the road.

This book walks through it in forty short poems, in five parts: the Son greater than all, the rest that remains, the great high priest, the heroes of faith, and the race toward a kingdom that can’t be shaken. Each poem sits beside a picture and under a single line of Scripture. The pictures stay with the things the letter touches—a lamp, an anchor, a basin, an open door—and leave the faces to your imagination.

The poems are not the Bible. They are one reader's response to it. Open the letter to the Hebrews alongside this book, and let the real words have the last word.

paintings.title: many ways
paintings.epigraph: “has at the end of these days spoken to us by his Son”
paintings.poem:
he spoke in pieces
for a long time.

a burning bush.
a still small voice.
a prophet's bent back,
a clay pot smashed
on purpose in the street.

a word here.
a dream there.

the fathers kept every scrap
and waited.

then, at the end of these days,
he stopped sending messages

and sent his Son.
paintings.reflectionPrompt: In the quiet after the noise, what gentle truth from Hebrews 1:1–2 (“and sent his Son”) is asking for your unhurried attention today?

paintings.title: radiance
paintings.epigraph: “His Son is the radiance of his glory, the very image of his substance”
paintings.poem:
you can't look at the sun.

but you can stand in the light
that comes from it,

feel it on your face,
watch it turn a grey field
to gold.

the light is not
a copy of the sun.
it is the sun,
reaching you.

that is what the Son is
to the Father.

you have never seen God.

you have seen
his morning.
paintings.reflectionPrompt: As you linger with “radiance” (Hebrews 1:3)—where the poem notes, “you have seen his morning”—where do you recognize this same moment on your own walk today?

paintings.title: like a garment
paintings.epigraph: “but you are the same. Your years won’t fail.”
paintings.poem:
the sky will wear thin
like an old coat.

the mountains, the stars,
all of it
folded up someday
and put away.

everything you know
is getting older.

except him.

your years won't fail,
the psalm says to the Son.

so when the fabric
of your life
wears through at the elbows,

remember who is holding it.
paintings.reflectionPrompt: As you linger with “like a garment” (Hebrews 1:10–12)—where the poem notes, “remember who is holding it”—where do you recognize this same moment on your own walk today?

paintings.title: drift
paintings.epigraph: “Therefore we ought to pay greater attention to the things that were heard, lest perhaps we drift away.”
paintings.poem:
no one decides to drift.

you just stop
checking the rope.

the water is calm.
the evening is kind.
the shore gets farther
an inch at a time.

pay attention,
the letter says,

not because the sea is angry,

because it is so quiet.
paintings.reflectionPrompt: As you linger with “drift” (Hebrews 2:1)—where the poem notes, “because it is so quiet”—where do you recognize this same moment on your own walk today?

paintings.title: what is man
paintings.epigraph: “What is man, that you think of him?”
paintings.poem:
look up long enough
and you feel
about the size of a pebble.

what are we,
that you would even think of us?

the answer came
in a body.

he was made
a little lower than the angels,
low enough
to taste death
for everyone.

that is how much
you are thought of.
paintings.reflectionPrompt: As you linger with “what is man” (Hebrews 2:6–9)—where the poem notes, “that is how much you are thought of”—where do you recognize this same moment on your own walk today?

paintings.title: not ashamed
paintings.epigraph: “he is not ashamed to call them brothers”
paintings.poem:
he knows your family.

he knows the arguments,
the empty chair,
the name nobody says.

he knows you.

and he pulls out a seat
and says to anyone listening:

this one's with me.
my brother.
my sister.

not ashamed.

not even a little.
paintings.reflectionPrompt: In the quiet after the noise, what gentle truth from Hebrews 2:11 (“not even a little”) is asking for your unhurried attention today?

paintings.title: his house
paintings.epigraph: “W e are his house, if we hold fast our confidence and the glorying of our hope firm to the end.”
paintings.poem:
every house
has a builder.

stone on stone,
the line held true,
the mallet's patient knock.

Moses was faithful
in the house
like a trusted servant.

the Son is faithful
over it.

and the house
is not a building.

it's you.
it's us.

still going up.
paintings.reflectionPrompt: As you pause at the threshold of “his house” (Hebrews 3:4–6), what closed place in your life is waiting for you to open to His presence?

paintings.title: today
paintings.epigraph: “T oday if you will hear his voice, don’t harden your hearts”
paintings.poem:
not yesterday.
you can't hear him there.

not tomorrow.
it hasn't come.

only today,
this plain one,
with its dishes and its traffic,

where a voice
might be speaking
under all the noise.

clay stays soft
while it's wet.

listen
while it's today.
paintings.reflectionPrompt: In the quiet after the noise, what gentle truth from Hebrews 3:15 (“listen while it's today”) is asking for your unhurried attention today?

paintings.title: day by day
paintings.epigraph: “but exhort one another day by day”
paintings.poem:
nobody hardens overnight.

it happens slowly,
one small no,
one quiet lie
you tell yourself.

so the cure
is slow too.

a word at the door.
a hand on the shoulder.
come back tomorrow.

day by day,
as long as it's called
today,

keep each other soft.
paintings.reflectionPrompt: As you linger with “day by day” (Hebrews 3:13)—where the poem notes, “keep each other soft”—where do you recognize this same moment on your own walk today?

paintings.title: forty years
paintings.epigraph: “W e see that they weren’t able to enter in because of unbelief.”
paintings.poem:
they saw the sea split.
they ate bread
that fell from the sky.

and still,
at the edge of the land,
they were afraid
to go in.

forty years
of walking in circles
around a promise.

not because God's hand was short.

because they would not
put their weight on it.
paintings.reflectionPrompt: What anxious weight can you place into the hands of the One who says, “Be still” and walks beside you in Hebrews 3:16–19?

paintings.title: mixed with faith
paintings.epigraph: “the word they heard didn’t profit them, because it wasn’t mixed with faith by those who heard.”
paintings.poem:
flour on the board.
water in the jug.

good things,
both of them.

but they won't become bread
sitting side by side.

the good news came to them
the same as us.

they heard it.
they didn't knead it in.

a promise is a gift.

faith is the hands.
paintings.reflectionPrompt: As you linger with “mixed with faith” (Hebrews 4:2)—where the poem notes, “faith is the hands”—where do you recognize this same moment on your own walk today?

paintings.title: the seventh day
paintings.epigraph: “God rested on the seventh day from all his works”
paintings.poem:
he didn't rest
because he was tired.

he rested
because it was finished.

and good.

he stepped back
from the whole shining world

and let it be.

there's a kind of rest
that isn't sleep.

it's the rest
of the one who knows
the work is done.
paintings.reflectionPrompt: Where is God inviting you to set down your work today and rest in what He has already finished (Hebrews 4:4)?

paintings.title: a Sabbath rest
paintings.epigraph: “There remains therefore a Sabbath rest for the people of God.”
paintings.poem:
you have been
so busy
proving yourself.

earning your place.
keeping up.

there remains a rest,
the letter says,

like a room
already made up,
a table already set,
the door left open.

you don't build it.

you walk in,
and take off your shoes,
and stop.
paintings.reflectionPrompt: Where is God inviting you to set down your work today and rest in what He has already finished (Hebrews 4:9–10)?

paintings.title: sharper
paintings.epigraph: “For the word of God is living and active, and sharper than any two-edged sword”
paintings.poem:
it's lying on the table.

no one is holding it.

and still
it catches the light
along both edges.

this word goes
past the face you wear

to the thought
you haven't said out loud.

it doesn't cut
to wound.

it cuts to find
what needs healing.
paintings.reflectionPrompt: As you linger with “sharper” (Hebrews 4:12)—where the poem notes, “it cuts to find what needs healing”—where do you recognize this same moment on your own walk today?

paintings.title: touched
paintings.epigraph: “we don’t have a high priest who can’t be touched with the feeling of our infirmities”
paintings.poem:
he was hungry in the desert.
tired at a well.
he wept at a grave.

he knew what it was
to be pulled
toward the wrong thing,

and he didn't go.

so when you come to him
with your weakness,

he doesn't read it
off a chart.

he remembers.
paintings.reflectionPrompt: As you linger with “touched” (Hebrews 4:15)—where the poem notes, “he remembers”—where do you recognize this same moment on your own walk today?

paintings.title: the throne of grace
paintings.epigraph: “Let’s therefore draw near with boldness to the throne of grace”
paintings.poem:
most thrones
you approach
bowing, afraid,
hoping not to be noticed.

this one
you walk up to.

boldly.

not because you're good enough,

but because of what
the throne is made of.

grace.

and what you'll find there
is exactly
what you came needing.

help,
in time.
paintings.reflectionPrompt: What anxious weight can you place into the hands of the One who says, “Be still” and walks beside you in Hebrews 4:16?

paintings.title: strong crying
paintings.epigraph: “having offered up prayers and petitions with strong crying and tears”
paintings.poem:
he didn't pray
politely.

he prayed with loud cries.
with tears.

the Son of God
on his face
among the olive trees.

and the letter says
he was heard.

so you can cry out too.

loud is not
a lack of faith.

sometimes it's
the whole of it.
paintings.reflectionPrompt: As you linger with “strong crying” (Hebrews 5:7–8)—where the poem notes, “sometimes it's the whole of it”—where do you recognize this same moment on your own walk today?

paintings.title: not forgotten
paintings.epigraph: “For God is not unrighteous, so as to forget your work and the labor of love”
paintings.poem:
the meals you carried.
the floor you swept
after everyone went home.

the visit
no one saw.
the thank-you
that never came.

you thought
it disappeared.

it didn't.

God is not the kind
of God
who forgets.

he's keeping
every bowl.
paintings.reflectionPrompt: As you linger with “not forgotten” (Hebrews 6:10)—where the poem notes, “he's keeping every bowl”—where do you recognize this same moment on your own walk today?

paintings.title: anchor
paintings.epigraph: “This hope we have as an anchor of the soul, a hope both sure and steadfast”
paintings.poem:
an anchor doesn't
stop the storm.

the waves still come.
the boat still rocks.
you still feel
every swell.

but you don't
go anywhere.

this hope
is tied to something
you can't see,

on the far side
of the veil,
where Jesus already went.

the rope goes
deeper than the weather.
paintings.reflectionPrompt: As you linger with “anchor” (Hebrews 6:19)—where the poem notes, “the rope goes deeper than the weather”—where do you recognize this same moment on your own walk today?

paintings.title: to the uttermost
paintings.epigraph: “he lives forever to make intercession for them”
paintings.poem:
the old priests
grew old.

they died,
and someone else
put on the robes.

not this one.

he lives forever,

and forever
he is saying your name
to the Father.

on the nights
you can't pray,
he is praying.

that's what the uttermost means.

there is no far
he can't reach.
paintings.reflectionPrompt: As you linger with “to the uttermost” (Hebrews 7:24–25)—where the poem notes, “there is no far he can't reach”—where do you recognize this same moment on your own walk today?

paintings.title: no more
paintings.epigraph: “I will remember their sins and lawless deeds no more.”
paintings.poem:
he knows everything.

and he has chosen
to forget
one thing.

not the way we forget,
by accident,
the keys,
a birthday.

on purpose.

he won't bring it up.
he won't keep a list.

the law is written
on your heart now.

your sins
aren't written anywhere.
paintings.reflectionPrompt: As you linger with “no more” (Hebrews 8:10–12)—where the poem notes, “your sins aren't written anywhere”—where do you recognize this same moment on your own walk today?

paintings.title: once a year
paintings.epigraph: “into the second the high priest alone, once in the year”
paintings.poem:
the lamp in the first room
never went out.

the bread
was always on the table.

but behind the curtain
only one man went,
one day a year,
carefully.

everyone else
stood outside
and waited to see
if he'd come back.

that was the closest
anyone could get.

it was never meant
to stay that way.
paintings.reflectionPrompt: In the quiet after the noise, what gentle truth from Hebrews 9:6–7 (“it was never meant to stay that way”) is asking for your unhurried attention today?

paintings.title: the veil
paintings.epigraph: “a new and living way, through the veil”
paintings.poem:
for all those years
the curtain said:
this far.

then he went through it.

not around.
not over.

through,
his own body
the way in.

now the light
spills out into the hall

and the curtain says
something new.

come in.

come all the way in.
paintings.reflectionPrompt: As you linger with “the veil” (Hebrews 10:19–22)—where the poem notes, “come all the way in”—where do you recognize this same moment on your own walk today?

paintings.title: assurance
paintings.epigraph: “Now faith is assurance of things hoped for, proof of things not seen.”
paintings.poem:
a seed doesn't look
like a harvest.

it looks like
a dry little nothing
in your palm.

you plant it anyway.

you water ground
that shows you nothing.

you wait.

that is faith.

not pretending
you can see it.

planting like
you already know.
paintings.reflectionPrompt: In the quiet after the noise, what gentle truth from Hebrews 11:1 (“planting like you already know”) is asking for your unhurried attention today?

paintings.title: Abel
paintings.epigraph: “through it he, being dead, still speaks.”
paintings.poem:
he didn't say much,
that we know of.

he kept sheep.
he gave God
the best of them.

and his life
was short.

but the letter says
he is still speaking.

a gift given
with a whole heart

goes on talking
long after you're gone.
paintings.reflectionPrompt: As you linger with “Abel” (Hebrews 11:4)—where the poem notes, “goes on talking long after you're gone”—where do you recognize this same moment on your own walk today?

paintings.title: Enoch
paintings.epigraph: “before his translation he had been well pleasing to God.”
paintings.poem:
he walked with God

day after day
the way you'd walk
with a friend,

no hurry,
no destination
anyone else could see.

and then one day
he wasn't found.

the path just went on
into the light.

some people
walk so close with God
that heaven
is just the next step.
paintings.reflectionPrompt: As you linger with “Enoch” (Hebrews 11:5)—where the poem notes, “that heaven is just the next step”—where do you recognize this same moment on your own walk today?

paintings.title: Noah
paintings.epigraph: “being warned about things not yet seen, moved with godly fear, prepared a ship for the saving of his house”
paintings.poem:
no clouds.
no rain.

just a man
building a boat
in a dry field,

plank by plank.

he was warned
about things not yet seen,

and he believed
the warning
more than the weather.

some faith
looks foolish

until it's the only thing
still floating.
paintings.reflectionPrompt: As you linger with “Noah” (Hebrews 11:7)—where the poem notes, “until it's the only thing still floating”—where do you recognize this same moment on your own walk today?

paintings.title: not knowing where
paintings.epigraph: “He went out, not knowing where he went.”
paintings.poem:
he packed the tents.

he said goodbye
to the only country he knew.

where are you going?
the neighbors asked.

he didn't know.

he knew
who had called him.

for the rest of his life
he lived in tents,

looking for a city
with foundations,

whose builder
is God.
paintings.reflectionPrompt: As you linger with “not knowing where” (Hebrews 11:8–10)—where the poem notes, “whose builder is God”—where do you recognize this same moment on your own walk today?

paintings.title: Sarah
paintings.epigraph: “she counted him faithful who had promised.”
paintings.poem:
she had laughed at it once.

far too old,
far too late,
too many years
of empty arms.

but somewhere
she decided
the promise
wasn't about her.

it was about him.

and he had never
broken his word.

so there was a cradle
in the tent.

and laughter,
the other kind.
paintings.reflectionPrompt: As you linger with “Sarah” (Hebrews 11:11)—where the poem notes, “and laughter, the other kind”—where do you recognize this same moment on your own walk today?

paintings.title: strangers and pilgrims
paintings.epigraph: “they were strangers and pilgrims on the earth.”
paintings.poem:
they died
without getting there.

they saw it
from far off
and waved,

the way you wave at someone
coming up the road.

they could have gone back.
there was time.

they didn't.

they wanted
a better country.

and God
was not ashamed
to be called their God.
paintings.reflectionPrompt: As you linger with “strangers and pilgrims” (Hebrews 11:13–16)—where the poem notes, “was not ashamed to be called their God”—where do you recognize this same moment on your own walk today?

paintings.title: Moses
paintings.epigraph: “for he endured, as seeing him who is invisible.”
paintings.poem:
he could have had
all of it.

the palace.
the river barges.
the name.

he walked away
toward the sand
and the slaves.

what did he see
that the palace didn't?

the letter says
he kept going
as seeing
him who is invisible.

that was enough
to trade a kingdom for.
paintings.reflectionPrompt: As you linger with “Moses” (Hebrews 11:24–27)—where the poem notes, “that was enough to trade a kingdom for”—where do you recognize this same moment on your own walk today?

paintings.title: Rahab
paintings.epigraph: “Rahab the prostitute didn’t perish with those who were disobedient, having received the spies in peace.”
paintings.poem:
she wasn't anybody's
idea of a hero.

a woman with a past,
a house in the wall.

but she heard
what God had done,

and she believed it
before anyone asked her to.

she opened the door.
she hid the strangers.
she hung the scarlet cord.

and her name
is in the list,

right there
next to Moses.
paintings.reflectionPrompt: As you linger with “Rahab” (Hebrews 11:31)—where the poem notes, “right there next to Moses”—where do you recognize this same moment on your own walk today?

paintings.title: cloud of witnesses
paintings.epigraph: “seeing we are surrounded by so great a cloud of witnesses”
paintings.poem:
the stands are full.

Abel.
Enoch.
Noah with his hands
still rough from the wood.

Abraham, Sarah.
Moses. Rahab.

all of them
who ran
and didn't see
the finish.

they're not watching
to judge your time.

they know
how hard this lap is.

they're the ones
cheering.
paintings.reflectionPrompt: As you linger with “cloud of witnesses” (Hebrews 12:1)—where the poem notes, “they're the ones cheering”—where do you recognize this same moment on your own walk today?

paintings.title: run
paintings.epigraph: “looking to Jesus, the author and perfecter of faith”
paintings.poem:
put it down,
the weight you've carried
since the start.

run with patience,
not speed.

and don't watch
your feet.

look up the road
to the one
who already finished it

and is waiting
at the end.
paintings.reflectionPrompt: In the quiet after the noise, what gentle truth from Hebrews 12:1–2 (“and is waiting at the end”) is asking for your unhurried attention today?

paintings.title: a father's discipline
paintings.epigraph: “afterward it yields the peaceful fruit of righteousness to those who have been trained by it.”
paintings.poem:
a gardener
ties the young tree
to a stake.

it doesn't feel
like love
to the tree.

but come summer,
straight branches,
fruit.

the hard seasons
aren't proof
he's left you.

they're proof
you're his.
paintings.reflectionPrompt: As you linger with “a father's discipline” (Hebrews 12:7–11)—where the poem notes, “they're proof you're his”—where do you recognize this same moment on your own walk today?

paintings.title: feeble knees
paintings.epigraph: “Therefore lift up the hands that hang down and the feeble knees”
paintings.poem:
you're tired.
of course you are.

this letter knows it.

so it doesn't say
run faster.

it says
lift up your hands.
steady your knees.

clear the stones
off the path,

so the ones behind you
who are limping

can make it too.
paintings.reflectionPrompt: As you linger with “feeble knees” (Hebrews 12:12–13)—where the poem notes, “can make it too”—where do you recognize this same moment on your own walk today?

paintings.title: can't be shaken
paintings.epigraph: “receiving a Kingdom that can’t be shaken”
paintings.poem:
one day
he will shake
everything.

the heavens.
the earth.
all the things we built
to feel safe.

and what can fall
will fall.

let it.

you've been given
something else.

a kingdom
that doesn't move
when the ground does.
paintings.reflectionPrompt: As you linger with “can't be shaken” (Hebrews 12:26–28)—where the poem notes, “that doesn't move when the ground does”—where do you recognize this same moment on your own walk today?

paintings.title: strangers at the door
paintings.epigraph: “Don’t forget to show hospitality to strangers, for in doing so, some have entertained angels without knowing it.”
paintings.poem:
set another place.

pour the water.
bring the bread.

you don't know
who's coming up the road.

a tired traveler.
a neighbor.
someone with nowhere else.

or someone
heaven sent.

some opened the door
and never knew.

open it anyway.
paintings.reflectionPrompt: As you pause at the threshold of “strangers at the door” (Hebrews 13:2), what closed place in your life is waiting for you to open to His presence?

paintings.title: never leave
paintings.epigraph: “I will in no way leave you, neither will I in any way forsake you.”
paintings.poem:
when the money's gone.
when the house is quiet.
when the ones you counted on
have moved away.

he said it
more than once,
so you would remember.

not in any way.

not ever.

you can be content
with a little

when the one thing
you can't lose

is sitting up with you
in the dark.
paintings.reflectionPrompt: As you linger with “never leave” (Hebrews 13:5–6)—where the poem notes, “is sitting up with you in the dark”—where do you recognize this same moment on your own walk today?

paintings.title: the same
paintings.epigraph: “Jesus Christ is the same yesterday, today, and forever.”
paintings.poem:
the world will change.
your address,
your face in the mirror.

but the one
who held the children,
who touched the leper,
who walked out of the tomb,

has not changed
a single thing
about how he loves you.

yesterday.

today.

and every morning
after this one.
paintings.reflectionPrompt: As you linger with “the same” (Hebrews 13:8)—where the poem notes, “and every morning after this one”—where do you recognize this same moment on your own walk today?
